item.title: 25 houses burnt, over 100 people displaced are still waiting for justice on Kairuru Island
item.description: It has been nine months since destruction followed a suspicious death that left 25 houses torched and more than 100 people, including children, displaced. The victims are still waiting for police intervention and provincial government support on Kairuru Island, East Sepik. Displaced families from Rumlal, Surai, Shovir and Sislal villages met with PNG Tribal Foundation last Thursday to find solutions to help them return to their land and bring police for investigations. item.title: Tribal Foundation runs screening program on Mushu Island
item.description: It was the first time an awareness program on sorcery accusations and domestic violence was brought to Mushu Island last week. PNG Tribal Foundation conducted its screening program, Senisim Pasin, a community outreach initiative through documentary screening, last Friday in Sup Village. The event saw more than 60 villagers, both young and old turn up in large numbers. Many described the program as eye-opening and expressed their gratitude for the opportunity. item.title: Collaborative food processing training empowers local farmers and entrepreneurs in Buka
item.description: A week-long food processing training workshop, aimed at enhancing local capabilities in value-added production, concluded successfully at the BACRA Laboratory in Kubu, Buka. The initiative, a collaboration between Volunteer Service Abroad (VSA), BACRA, and the Department of Primary Industry (DPI), drew over 20 participants, including local farmers, agricultural advocates, and aspiring entrepreneurs.
